item.title: 'I was a big fan of Mark Cavendish when he raced for this team' – Soudal-QuickStep sign versatile Tim Torn Teutenberg from Lidl-Trek
item.content:encoded: Soudal-QuickStep have announced their first new transfer for the 2027 season, with versatile German rider Tim Torn Teutenberg joining from Lidl-Trek on a two-year deal. Teutenberg had raced for Lidl-Trek's WorldTour team since 2025, having impressed as an U23 rider on their development squad, winning Paris-Roubaix Espoirs and the Olympia's Tour in 2024.Since turning professional, the 24-year-old has yet to land a victory, but has shown great promise in sprints – both going for his own ambitions and as a lead-out, time trials, and as a potential Classics star. "I'm delighted to join this team. I’ve admired Soudal Quick-Step since I was young and was a big fan of Mark Cavendish when he raced for The Wolfpack," said Teutenberg on the team's website. "It’s a squad with an extraordinary legacy in the Classics, which are the races where I hope to keep improving. At the same time, I also want to develop as a sprinter, so next season will be about finding the right balance between the two."The team will be known as Soudal Safety Jogger when the German first pins on a race number for them in 2027, with development team rider Ceriel Desal the only other confirmed new arrival for next season.But he should also get his chance to develop as a sprinter at the races they aren't at, with hopes of matching some of his best results as an U23 rider in the Classics: "I’ve never raced Paris-Roubaix since turning professional, but I hope that by joining this team I’ll get the opportunity to do so and support the squad as best I can in the fight for a great result on the French cobbles.""Tim has already shown that he is a very versatile rider. He has the speed to compete in bunch sprints, he can perform well in the Classics, and he has also demonstrated his qualities in time trials and on the track," said team CEO Jurgen Fore. "That versatility, combined with his ambition to improve and his strong work ethic, makes him an exciting rider for the future."We believe he is a great fit for our team and our philosophy. He is still young, eager to learn and ready to take the next step in his career. We are looking forward to working with him over the coming seasons and helping him continue his development. We are confident that, together, we can achieve some great things."

item.title: As it happened: Tour de France Femmes stage 6 sparks attacks, a GC chase and close sprint finish
item.content:encoded: Support our unrivalled coverage of the Tour de France Femmes and women's cycling by subscribing to Cyclingnews. In return, you get unlimited access to high-quality journalism, with breaking news, race analysis, and expert insight from inside the women's peloton. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go!This is the live coverage of stage 7: Kim le Court Pienaar (Mau) AG Insurance-SoudalCedrine Kerbaol (Fra) EF Education-OatlyPuck Pieterse (Ned) Fenix-Premier TechSarah van Dam (Can) Visma-Lease a BikeCélia Gery (Fra) FDJ United-SUEZLiane Lippert (Ger) Movistar TeamElisa Longo Borghini (Ita) UAE Team L'IMADRiejanne Markus (Ned) Lidl-TrekDominika Wlodarczyk (Pol) UAE Team L'IMADNoemi Ruegg (Swi) EF Education-OatlyMarlen Reusser (Swi) Movistar TeamDemi Vollering (Ned) FDJ United-SUEZKatarzyna Niewiadoma-Phinney (Pol) Canyon-SRAMElisa Longo Borghini (Ita) UAE Team L'IMADAntonia Niedermaier (Ger) Canyon-SRAMDominika Wlodarczyk (Pol) UAE Team L'IMADIsabella Holmgren (Can) Lidl-TrekCedrine Kerbaol (Fra) EF Education-OatlyKim le Court Pienaar (Mau) AG Insurance-SoudalPaula Blasi Cairol (Spa) UAE Team L'IMADBonjour and welcome to the Cyclingnews live coverage of stage 6 of the Tour de France Femmes.Like every day, we will have full live coverage, from the sign-on until beyond the finish line, with race updates, analysis, rider quotes and race photographs. The riders are currently signing on in Montbrison, in the the Loire department in central France, east of Lyon. Riders always find time for autographs.This is a detailed stage preview of stage 6. It is a medium-mountain stage that covers 153.4km, passing through the eastern part of the Massif Central on narrow roads, almost always either climbing or descending. The 153.4km stage includes 2600m of altitude gain, 6 categorised climbs and many others.Pauline Ferrand-Prévot endured a bad day on stage 5 but is smiling on the sign-on podium today. I can't have any regrets.I'm going to fight on and try to get the best possible result. Thanks to the public for all their incredible support.This was our story with Pauline Ferrand-Prévot reaction after stage 5.It's another hot day in France, with temperatures for the stage expected to touch 32C. We're five minutes from the roll-out of the stage in Montbrison. The riders face 153.4km in the saddle, with a 5km neutralised sector.We'll have all the action from every km until the finish in Tournon-sur-Rhône. The race speaker does a countdown ands lets out his long "C'est Parti.....!" It's great to see Chiara Consonni race on despite a nasty crash early on stage 5.She joked she has less skin but two stitches in her knee. Following her strong TT and her excellent performance in the hills on stage 5, Marlen Reusser (Movistar) is still in the yellow jersey.But she has just a 12-second lead on Demi Vollering (FDJ United-Suez) and 1:17 on Katarzyna Niewiadoma-Phinney (Canyon-SRAM). They will surely fight for every second today before the big show down on Mont Ventoux on Friday.There are 10, 6 and 4 bonus seconds up for grabs at the finish line in Tournon-sur-Rhône, as well as 6, 4 and 2 seconds at the Bonus Point located at Saint-Barthélemy-le-Plain after 144.2km. This was the roll out and now the stage has officially started. No attacks from the moment the start flag was waved.134 riders start the 6th stage of the 2026 Tour de France Femmes at exactly 13:46.Two riders did not start: Barbara Malcotti (Human Powered Health) and Monica Trinca Colonel (Liv AlUla Jayco). For now the race is gruppo compatto but we are expecting attacks. After the intense racing on stage 5 and with Ventoux coming up on Friday, there is a sense in the peloton that a breakaway might have a chance today. We expect the first attacks to come on the early climbs.Josie Nelson (Picnic) is the first attacker of the day. The riders start the double whammy of the 1.4km Côte de Périgneux and the 2.7km Côte de la Prunerie. Riders are already being dropped as Josie Nelson is caught. So far the action is at the back of the bunch, rather than the front, with more and more riders dropped.At the top of the Côte de Périgneux, Puck 'polka-dot' Pieterse again kicks away to score 2 QOM points. Pieterse took the polka-dot jersey by chance but has now opted to chase every point. She will have to ride aggressive today and at the weekend to hold off the GC riders, who will score points as they fight for overall victory.As the Côte de la Prunerie second climb begins, we have some real attacks.Loes Adegeest (Lidl-Trek), Nikola Nosková (Cofidis), Katrine Aalerud (Uno-X Mobility) have opened a 20-second gap. Sadly the speed means that Eleonora Ciabocco (Picnic) was in pain and she has abandoned.Loes Adegeest (Lidl-Trek), Nikola Nosková (Cofidis) and Katrine Aalerud (Uno-X Mobility) have pushed their gap ut to 40 seconds.Puck Pieterse has extended her lead as QOM.Human Powered Health is leading the peloton, trying to keep the breakaway under control.Célia Gery (FDJ United-Suez) accelerates from the peloton. The peloton is 1:00 behind now. Other riders are accelerating but Anna Van der Breggen and Marianne Vos have been dropped. Mental strength is also important in the Tour.The race is climbing higher into the hills, with the Côte de Praneuf looming. Just like stage 5, there is little chance to recover bewtten each clmib, descent and the next climb. Up front, Loes Adegeest (Lidl-Trek), Nikola Nosková (Cofidis), Katrine Aalerud (Uno-X Mobility) are working smoothly together. They have extended their lead out to 2:20 now. The pace in the peloton has eased on the plateau roads and that allowed van der Breggen and other riders to get back on.There 114 riders in the peloton, 3 on the attack and a gruppetto of 15 riders at 5:00. Visma-Lease a Bike have been forced to rewrite their Tour de France Femmes race strategy after defending champion Pauline Ferrand-Prévot lost a further 2:35 on stage 5, with Femke de Vries now the team's best-placed rider in the GC.The riders have covered 1300 m of the total 2600m of elevation gain they face today.That indicates that the first part of the stage, the 60km covered so far, was harder that what is to come. However the next 50km are tough, with the 8.6km Col de Lalouvesc coming with 50km to go. First they face the short but steep Côte de Praneuf, then the road continues to climb upwards at a gradual pace. The race passed the intermediate sprint point a little earlier. Loes Adegeest (Lidl-Trek), Nikola Nosková (Cofidis), Katrine Aalerud (Uno-X Mobility) took the first three places but Lorena Wiebes (SD Worx) was near the front of the peloton, was 5th over the line and so scored 13 more points. She leads the green jersey competition with 144 points, with her teammate Lotte Kopecky second with 79 points. Wiebes, thanks to her stage wins and other points, surely only has to finish the Tour to win the green jersey. EF Education-Oatly are chasing stage victories this year. They missed the three-roider attack and so are chasing, with Henrietta Christie working on the front. He efforts have helped reduce the gap to 1:50. EF will try to launch a riders across or into any more serious attack later in the stage. We can see Loes Adegeest (Lidl-Trek), Nikola Nosková (Cofidis), Katrine Aalerud (Uno-X Mobility) working smoothly together.With EF's pink jersey's on the front of the chasing peloton. There is a sense that this is the big move of the day, because EF don't want it to be. August 6, 2026 – 10:02 AMFenix-Premier Tech are also helping with the chase to try to help Puck Pieterse take as many QOM points as possible. Nikola Nosková (Cofidis) is in the attack and has so-far picked-up 5 points. That puts her on 19, with Pieterse on 39. Pieterse wants to score maximum points on the Cat 2 Col de Lalouvesc that awards, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 points. Nosková may not be a major threat to Pieterse but she needs to hold off other GC climbers like Demi Vollering, who could take the polka.-dot jersey on the way to overall victory in the Tour.For example, 15 points are awarded at the finish on Mont Ventoux.August 6, 2026 – 10:03 AMEF are bringing the break back, with Kirsten Faulkner on the front and even off the front. The gap is just 35 seconds now. August 6, 2026 – 10:12 AMMischa Bredewold (SD Worx) is also helping the chase, a sign that Lotte Kopecky could try to go in a later attack.The trio ahead seem to know their momnt is coming to end, with the gap at 30 seconds and Nikola Nosková (Cofidis) distanced due to Loes Adegeest (Lidl-Trek) upping the speed.August 6, 2026 – 10:17 AMSadly Fenix-Premier Tech) has abandoned the TDFF.August 6, 2026 – 10:24 AMThe gap to Loes Adegeest (Lidl-Trek) and Katrine Aalerud (Uno-X Mobility) remains at 30 seconds, as the peloton takes the descent on country roads with caution.Marlen Reusser moves to the front at one point to show she wants a steady pace. The road is about to climb with the 8.6km Col de Lalouvesc, that rises at 5%.Could Demi Vollering try an attack? In theory yes but Reusser will surely be able to match her on a 5% climb. August 6, 2026 – 10:27 AMAs the Col de Lalouvesc begins, Loes Adegeest (Lidl-Trek) drops Katrine Aalerud (Uno-X Mobility). The GC peloton is only 20 seconds behind. Get ready for more attacks. August 6, 2026 – 10:31 AMThe peloton is splitting, with Pauline Ferrand-Prévot at the back.Lorena Wiebes is dropped but she had fought to try to stay up front in the hope the race came back together. August 6, 2026 – 10:39 AMWorld champion Magdeleine Vallieres (EF) is setting the pace and splitting the GC peloton.She helped sweep up the peloton and only 35 riders are left up front.Kim Le Court-Pienaar is 40 second down. This could be another GC day. August 6, 2026 – 10:40 AMLotte Kopecky is up front but Anna van der Breggen has been dropped and is riding with Wiebes. Any GC hopes she had are over now.August 6, 2026 – 10:41 AMPaula Balsi (UAE) attacks with 3km to climb.August 6, 2026 – 10:43 AMIt will be fascinating to see what Blasi does next and how she races.Can she ride as a leader? Can she attack again? Can she try to win the stage? There are so many legitimate questions that the team and the UAE riders have failed to answer.August 6, 2026 – 10:45 AMBlasi is pulled back and so EF lead again, with Kristen Faulkner doing the work with 2 kilometres left to climb in the Col de Lalouvesc.French nartional chanmpion Célia Gery (FDJ United - SUEZ) is also on the front and controlling the racing for Vollering. August 6, 2026 – 10:47 AMKim Le Court-Pienaar is back in the GC peloton after the steeper gradients eased. The summit of the climb is near. Where is polka-dot Puck? August 6, 2026 – 10:49 AMPuck Pieterse kicks and she takes 5 points for the QOM jersey. Her teammates plays a sweeper role and picks-up 4 points. August 6, 2026 – 10:50 AMThere are 32 riders in the GC group and now they can enjoy 30k of descending roads until the last Côte de Boucieu-le-Roi climb with 20km to go.August 6, 2026 – 10:53 AMHave you voted in our daily poll at the top of the Live section? Will there be more GC drama on stage 6? August 6, 2026 – 10:54 AMEnjoying our live race coverage? Subscribe to Cyclingnews for an all-access pass to our unrivalled reporting of WorldTour racing, bike tech and exclusive in-depth features. Plus, access to the Cyclingnews app to follow the action on-the-go! August 6, 2026 – 11:02 AMVisma have Marion Bunel, Sarah Van Dam, Femke de Vries and Pauline Ferrand-Prévot in the GC group and so are active on the front. August 6, 2026 – 11:03 AMCélia Gery (FDJ United) is also aggressive and has attacked. August 6, 2026 – 11:06 AMA six-rider group has formed around Célia Gery. Some in the peloton are happy to let them go but others are not and attack in pursuit.August 6, 2026 – 11:08 AMIn the attack are Gery, Kerbaol, Lippert, Van Dam, Pieterse… and Paolo Longo Borghini.What happens now? Some teams will not work with the Italian champion.August 6, 2026 – 11:09 AMThere are only 26 riders in the GC group, so who will chase and why?The gap of the six is up to 20 seconds. August 6, 2026 – 11:10 AMCélia Gery is motivated because she is racing on home roads.August 6, 2026 – 11:12 AMThe presence of Longo Borghini probably means this attack will not stay away. She is a threat and sixth on GC. Indeed the gap is down to 15 seconds as the road flattens. August 6, 2026 – 11:13 AMSarah Van Dam (Visma-Lease a Bike), Cédrine Kerbaol (EF Education-EasyPost), Liane Lippert (Movistar Team), Elisa Longo Borghini (UAE Team L’Imad), Célia Gery (FDJ United-Suez) and Puck Pieterse (Fenix-Premier Tech).August 6, 2026 – 11:16 AMCanyon-SRAM, Lidl-Trek and SD Worx-Protime are not represented in the breakaway.So the white jersey Antonia Niedermaier is riding for Katarzyna Niewiadoma-Phinney. Se does not want to give Longo Borghini or Cédrine Kerbaol any time.The gap is at 30 seconds as the final 25km and final climb becomes a pursuit match. August 6, 2026 – 11:17 AMAugust 6, 2026 – 11:19 AMLidl-Trek are also helping with the chase.The pace is high and so riders are taking risks on the descent. Marlen Resusser (Movistar) even went off road onto the grass on a fast corner. August 6, 2026 – 11:23 AMThis attack and the fast chase is hurting lots of riders. August 6, 2026 – 11:24 AMThe gap is still 30 seconds as the Côte de Boucieu-le-Roi climb begins.Longo Borghini is leading the break and is hungry to gain time. August 6, 2026 – 11:27 AMFemke de Vries (Visma) has been dropped from the GC group. Shre is 8th on GC and, in theory, the new Visma GC leader after Ferrand-Prévot was distanced on stage 5. August 6, 2026 – 11:30 AMPuck Pieterse (Fenix-Premier Tech) leads over the top of the climb to score 5 more QOM points.The GC peloton is at 25 seconds but up front Cédrine Kerbaol (EF Education-EasyPost) attacks. August 6, 2026 – 11:31 AMThe riders are fighting a headwind and as Antonia Niedermaier eases up, the GC peloton eases. Lidl try to relaunch the chase but the gap is up to 40 seconds. August 6, 2026 – 11:33 AMElisa Longo Borghini (UAE Team L’Imad), Sarah Van Dam (Visma-Lease a Bike), Cédrine Kerbaol (EF Education-EasyPost) and Puck Pieterse (Fenix-Premier Tech) are all working hard in the attack but now Liane Lippert (Movistar Team) and Célia Gery (FDJ United-Suez) sit on, playing a GC tactic to protect Reusser's and Vollering's GC gaps. August 6, 2026 – 11:34 AMAugust 6, 2026 – 11:37 AMRiejanne Markus (Lidl) and Kim Le Court-Pienaar (AG Insurance) are trying to go across to the six.They moved at exactly the right time, the peloton seems to hsve let them go due to fatigue and a lack of rivals. The attack could soon become eight riders, with Le Court-Pienaar a fast finisher.August 6, 2026 – 11:38 AM8 riders up front, with only 19 riders in the GC peloton. But who will chase? And who will work with Le Court-Pienaar, knowing she is fast? Pro cycling really is like chess on wheels. August 6, 2026 – 11:41 AMAfter this short descent, there are 5km on the flat to the finish.They will decide if the break stays away.I think the 30-second gap is too big to close in such a short time by such a small GC group. This stage is now Le Court-Pienaar to lose. Surely someone will try to attack in the final kilometre and take a flyer. August 6, 2026 – 11:42 AMAugust 6, 2026 – 11:44 AMAs the descent eases, Le Court-Pienaar makes a clever attacks.Longo Borghini was boxed in for several vital seconds. She leads the chase but Le Court-Pienaar has a gap. August 6, 2026 – 11:46 AMLe Court-Pienaar is caught. Now what happens? Who attacks now? But if the eight attack each other, the GC group could close the gap.August 6, 2026 – 11:47 AMRiejanne Markus (Lidl) gets a gap but is closed down. August 6, 2026 – 11:47 AMIncredible the 8 are playing games in the last km.August 6, 2026 – 11:48 AMThe eight riders sprint it out. August 6, 2026 – 11:49 AMLe Court-Pienaar wins it! August 6, 2026 – 11:50 AMLe Court-Pienaar lead out the sprint, seemed like she was fading but found an extra kick to win. Not surprising she collapses on the ground in a mix of pain and emotion. August 6, 2026 – 11:52 AMThe official results show that Cédrine Kerbaol (EF Education-EasyPost) was second and Puck Pieterse (Fenix-Premier Tech) was third.August 6, 2026 – 11:56 AMWe have the first photos of the finish. August 6, 2026 – 12:03 PMThis is how close the sprint was.August 6, 2026 – 12:06 PMKim Le Court-Pienaar revealed that she suffered a bike problem before the last climb and so had to chase to get back on.The adrenaline then fueled her move to join the attack and win it.August 6, 2026 – 12:08 PMKim Le Court-Pienaar went deep to win.August 6, 2026 – 12:13 PMOf course, the GC did not change very much today, with Marlen Reusser and Demi Vollering finishing together. This is the new top five before the big showdown on the climb of Mont Ventoux on Friday.1. Marlen Reusser (Movistar )2. Demi Vollering (FDJ United-Suez), +123. Katarzyna Niewiadoma-Phinney (Canyon//SRAM), +1:174. Elisa Longo Borghini (UAE Team L’Imad), +2:285. Antonia Niedermaier (Canyon//SRAM), +2:40August 6, 2026 – 12:18 PMKim Le Court-Pienaar was emotional about her win."This was crazy. I had a mechanical on the on the downhill before the last climb, and I had to change bikes, and I was really far but my team was amazing," she said. "They brought me back slowly but surely to the bunch, and I got back on top of the last climb, which was a really big effort. And then I just tried to stay patient, try to recover from this big effort. Riejanne Markus and I bridged to the breakaway, and we got to the front. And they were not really cooperating, which is obvious. But I was happy to just still try.""I also got a gap in the last few kilometres, and Elisa closed me down. But then when Riejanne Markus made an attack from the back, I knew it was going to happen because that's the only way she can win a race like this. And I had to close the gap myself, and I was really, really dead. "I was on the limit. I can't believe I still had the legs to sprint. It was really hard. It was really this close before I could give up. I will never give up after this big effort my team did."August 6, 2026 – 12:18 PMKim Le Court-Pienaar finished second on stage 1 but had dropped out of the GC. "I've been really struggling since the TT day but I think this really makes our Tour," she said. "Of course, we've got GC ambitions, but winning a stage in a Tour de France is very special. You know, people don't really remember top 10, top five riders in Tour, but they do remember stage winners."August 6, 2026 – 12:25 PMEnjoying our live race coverage? Subscribe to Cyclingnews for an all-access pass to our unrivalled reporting of WorldTour racing, bike tech and exclusive in-depth features. Plus, access to the Cyclingnews app to follow the action on-the-go! August 6, 2026 – 12:28 PMWhat a day of racing and what a stage! Read our full stage report to understand the details of what happened, see the best race shots and results. August 6, 2026 – 12:36 PMOf course, it's the big one on Friday: Mont Ventoux day. The legendary "Giant of Provence”, Mont Ventoux crowns stage 7, after 146.8 kilometres and 3,500 metres of climbing from the start in La Voulte-sur-Rhône. As the Queen Stage of the 2026 Tour de France Femmes, it should deliver GC fireworks.This is our stage preview. Matilda Price and Dani Ostanek are on the ground in France and will soon have other special Ventoux news, interviews and features. Thanks for joining us for live coverage from stage 6. Check out our news and interviews from the stage and from all the other racing news. I'll be back on Friday to bring you full live coverage of the Mont Ventoux stage.

item.title: Isaac del Toro commits his future to UAE Team Emirates-XRG with new long-term contract extension
item.content:encoded: After his podium finish at the Tour de France, Mexican champion Isaac del Toro has extended his contract with UAE Team Emirates-XRG, committing his long-term future until 2031.He had already been confirmed to stay until 2029, but this updated deal makes him the rider with the longest commitment to cycling's top team, with even Tadej Pogačar and rising talents Pablo Torres and Jan Christen's contracts set to expire in 2030.Del Toro has become the secondary leader at UAE this season, backing up his runner-up finish from last year's Giro with third at his first Tour, all while supporting Pogačar to a fifth yellow jersey and winning a stage himself in Barcelona."I’m very happy to continue this journey with UAE Team Emirates-XRG. From the moment I joined the team, everybody has believed in me and given me the best environment to develop as both a rider and a person," said Del Toro on the team's website."Every season I’ve learned something new from my teammates and the people working around me, and I feel that I’m improving all the time."This team feels like home. We share the same ambition, the same passion for racing and the same desire to keep getting better. Signing long-term gives me a lot of confidence because I know I’m in the right place for my future."We’ve already achieved some amazing victories together, but I honestly believe the best is still to come. I’m excited to keep growing with this team and fighting for the biggest races in the world."

item.title: 'It was the first-ever climb I did' – Demi Vollering ready to head back to where it all began as Tour de France Femmes prepares for Mont Ventoux queen stage
item.author: cyclingnews@futurenet.com (Dani Ostanek)
item.content:encoded: Following her signal-of-intent victory in the hills of the Jura at the Tour de France Femmes, Demi Vollering is heading back to where it all began on Friday as the race makes its maiden voyage to the illustrious slopes of Mont Ventoux.The Giant of Provence made its name as a major climb of the men's Tour de France, featuring 18 times on the route since its inauguration in 1958. Other men's races, including Paris-Nice, the Critérium du Dauphiné, and Tour de la Provence, have also paid visits over the years.Meanwhile, the women's peloton has only raced up twice in recent times – at the 2016 Tour de L'Ardèche, and the 2022 Mont Ventoux Dénivelé Challenge.Anna Kiesenhofer soloed away in the early kilometres of the climb to take victory a decade ago, which was around the same time, Vollering was also discovering Ventoux for the first time.Back then, the Dutch racer's sporting focus still lay primarily on speed skating, though she was delving into road cycling before fully committing in 2018. Speaking at the post-stage press conference on Wednesday following her victory in Belleville-en-Beaujolais, Vollering discussed her Ventoux debut."It's a really nice climb, and it's a bit where it all started for me. So I'm really looking forward to this climb. It was the first-ever climb I did when I was younger," she said."It was 2018 the last time, I think. We always went in August. So, now it will be exactly 10 years ago that it was the first time, so it's quite cool."Vollering, who was emotional as she talked about those early visits to Ventoux, explained that she went on the trips with her speed skating training group after learning about the mountain via a recommendation from her coach."It was because I was still ice skating at that time, and we had a really nice group of friends," she said."Our trainers really made sure that we kept the fun, and one of the trainers always came every summer to Mont Ventoux with his wife. At one point he thought, 'I'll bring my training group with me.'"So then we went there with the bikes, and it was for the first time back then. Actually, after that, we did it every year for three years in a row. Then I became a pro, so I couldn't join anymore, but they kept on going."It's really nice, because I'm really still very close with this group, and they come every year to the Tour de France to support me, so it's really cool."'I'm just done. Let's just race' – Vollering ready to continue the yellow jersey battleOf course, the race-day experience of tackling the 15.7km climb will be poles apart from those friendly training rides. That 8.8% average gradient and wind-exposed lunar landscape will certainly feel different when Vollering is going head-to-head with her fellow top climbers, including Marlen Reusser (Movistar), Kasia Niewiadoma-Phinney (Canyon-SRAM), and Pauline Ferrand-Prévot (Visma-Lease a Bike).Still, Vollering, who has already ticked off stage wins on two other legendary Tour summits – the Col du Tourmalet and L'Alpe d'Huez – said she hopes she can enjoy Friday's ascent."It will bring back a lot of memories, I think. The feeling of riding a climb for the first time is super special – especially because I knew back then already that I was quite good at it, so I really enjoyed it. I really hope I can enjoy it again on the stage itself."I think still anything can happen. Mont Ventoux is a very, very hard climb, and last year, [Ferrand-Prévot] also took three minutes or more on almost all of us. So, we don't know what she is capable of on a long climb – it's just a different effort."Still, I would like to dream of yellow, of course, but we're not there yet. I cannot dream too big yet. I need to be focussed and tackle every day as a one-day stage race. Then, we will see all the way in Nice how it ends up."Vollering has been impatient for the GC action to kick off at this year's Tour. On the opening day's hilltop finish in Lausanne, she raced to third place to pick up four bonus seconds."Last year, I would wake up every morning thinking, 'Shit, another morning closer to the Tour.' And now I woke up every morning feeling super motivated and thinking, 'Yes, I feel good, and I'm looking forward to it'," she explained.On the evidence so far, Vollering is in top form. She followed up her outing in Lausanne with third in the Dijon time trial, shedding just 17 seconds to world champion Reusser, while yesterday brought that surge to a fourth career Tour stage win.With more hills on the way as the race hits the Ardèche on stage 6 before the Ventoux pilgrimage, the 'real racing', so to speak, is finally underway, and the GC battle is unfolding. Both Vollering and her FDJ United-SUEZ teammates are ready for the fight."Yesterday in the [team] meeting, I said, 'I'm just done. Let's just race,' because stage 2 and stage 3 were sometimes a bit boring, a bit slower, a bit waiting. Nobody really wanted to race, from my feeling," Vollering said."Also, maybe because of the heat, everybody was a bit scared, and maybe for stage 3, everybody was thinking already of the time trial. So, yeah, I was just ready to race, because that's the mindset I had coming into this Tour: to go full gas every day and not hesitate to make the race colourful."Also, in the beginning of the race, my teammates suffered a bit from the heat and maybe after the altitude to find their legs. But today was a day where everybody was in their form again, so we could really race and really enjoy it as a whole team."Support our unrivalled coverage of the Tour de France Femmes and women's cycling by subscribing to . In return, you get unlimited access to high-quality journalism, with breaking news, race analysis, and expert insight from inside the women's peloton. Plus, the app lets you follow the action wherever you go!
